question: Is cruelty wrong because God forbids it, or forbidden because it is wrong? What follows from the first answer?
answer: Morality becomes arbitrary command. If wrongness simply is being forbidden, a different command would have made cruelty right, and calling God good would only say God obeys himself. The other horn has its own cost: goodness then stands apart from God. Plato set the dilemma in the Euthyphro, and believers still debate it.
move: Ask whether a rule is good because commanded, or commanded because good.
ask: Is something I treat as right only right because someone with authority said so?
trap: More secure, since a divine source feels like the firmest ground.
reference: Plato, Euthyphro, in Five Dialogues, trans. Grube, rev. Cooper, Hackett, 2002
